newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana stock index slips in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Ghana stock index slips in thin trade.

text.p: Ghana's Stock Exchange index slipped in thin trade on Friday, with dealers saying investors were uneasy about political and economic trends.
The GSE All-Share Index, which has been trapped in a narrow range, fell 0.59 points to 376.33 from Wednesday's 376.92 points.
Dealers said they expected December 7 presidential and parliamentary elections to influence the mood in the market over the coming weeks.
Offers of 1.09 million shares far outstripped demand of 234,190 shares. Traders said institutional and foreign investors were absent, leaving the field largely to individual players.
Just 27,390 shares changed hands compared to 167,530 on Wednesday.
Accra Brewery limited (+20 cedis to 550 cedis), Mechanical Lloyd Company (+5 to 55 cedis) and CFAO (+1 to 18 cedis) were the only risers.
Mobil Oil Ghana Limited (-300 to 6,000 cedis), Unilever (-4 to 793 cedis) and Ghana Commercial Bank (-1 to 769 cedis) were the only fallers.
The week began on a slightly brighter note, with the GSE index rising 0.65 points to 376.88 on Monday.
Traders noted active domestic buying then, particularly from investment funds and a few individual investors, raising some hope that sentiment was about to improve.
